title: A Lean proof establishes the two-sum Ruzsa–Turjányi limit
summary: GPT-5.6 Sol proved that for a zero-density asymptotic additive basis, the ratio of the number of two-term sums up to 2N to the number of basis elements up to N tends to infinity. The statement is the two-sum variant of the older Ruzsa–Turjányi result for three-term sums.
ai_technology: GPT-5.6 Sol; h1 Lean proof-search harness

source_review.scope: Pinned Atlas Lean theorem and August 28 merge; h1 Table 1 and Appendix D; September separate formal proof and Formal Conjectures statement

evidence.tested: The formal proof encodes zero density and asymptotic additive-basis coverage. It applies the Plünnecke–Ruzsa inequality to control truncated sumsets.
evidence.unknown: This result concerns the density-zero two-sum variant. The originally posed bounded-limsup question in Erdős 337 is different and already has a counterexample.
evidence.ai_role: The h1 harness used GPT-5.6 Sol to generate a proof script with feedback from the Lean 4 checker.
